prompt:
You are a credit rating analyst. Using only the information below and general knowledge predating 2026-02-25, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify).
Valid answers (choose exactly one): AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Company information (as of 2026-02-25):
| Current ratio           | 0.42 |
| Retained earnings       | 261,693M |
| Current liabilities     | 2,559,605M |
| Current assets          | 1,067,083M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 303,243M |
| Total liabilities       | 3,107,151M |
| Total assets            | 3,410,394M |
| EBIT / operating income | 12,435M |
| Revenue                 | 49,691M |
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The company shows very high leverage (liabilities ~3.11T vs assets ~3.41T) and weak liquidity (current ratio 0.42), with substantial negative liquidity pressure despite positive EBIT and large retained earnings. These factors point to elevated default risk and speculative-grade credit quality, likely in the BB to B range, with BB being a conservative placement given some equity cushion but weak near-term liquidity.

DECISION: BB
